blocks.text: When the axes of two p-orbitals (i.e py or pz orbitals) are parallel to each other, they interact to form π molecular orbitals as shown in the diagram Figure 3.35. The bonding molecular orbitals π(2py) or π(2pz) have zero electron density on the nuclear axis (called the nodal plane). On the other hand, anti-bonding molecular orbitals π*(2py) and π*(2pz) have the least electron density in the inter-nuclear region.

blocks.alt: Six panels with + and - signs on the lobes. 2py - 2py gives an antibonding pi2p* with four lobes and a dotted node; 2py + 2py gives a bonding pi2p, one cloud above (+) and one below (-). 2pz - 2pz gives an antibonding pi2p*; 2pz + 2pz gives a bonding pi2p. 2px + 2px gives an antibonding sigma*2p with a node between the nuclei; 2px - 2px gives a bonding sigma2p with one large + region between the nuclei.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.35: Formation of sigma and pi MOs from px, py and pz orbitals (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.35; the printed caption shows a delta-like symbol for sigma).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed caption reads 'Formation of δ and π MOs'; δ (delta) should be σ (sigma). The figure shows σ and π molecular orbitals, as captioned above.
